children: Riyadh Air, Saudi Arabia’s national carrier wholly owned by the Public Investment Fund (PIF), has opened bookings for direct flights to Milan, with services set to begin on December 16.
The airline will operate four flights a week, making Milan its fifth European destination and 15th destination available for booking across its expanding network.
The new route marks another step in Riyadh Air’s global expansion strategy, connecting Saudi Arabia with major international business and cultural centers.
Riyadh Air CEO Tony Douglas said the launch of ticket sales to Milan marks another milestone in the carrier’s European expansion and will strengthen relations between Saudi Arabia and Italy.
He highlighted Milan’s role as a global center for business, culture, fashion and design, saying direct flights will improve connectivity while supporting trade and tourism.
The new service is also expected to enhance cooperation in luxury design and trade and boost tourism exchanges between the two countries.
